matching.title: Match the clue to the meaning
matching.subtitle: Tap a clue, then tap its meaning. The past perfect continuous (had been + -ing) shows duration before a past point or explains a past result; the past perfect shows a completed earlier action.

errorCorrection.title: Find the mistake
errorCorrection.subtitle: Each sentence has exactly one mistake. Tap the word you think is wrong. Twenty original sentences.

items.message: Leaving out ‘been’: the form is had been + -ing.
After ‘had been’ use the -ing form.
A completed earlier action: use the past perfect (had + past participle).
State verbs avoid the continuous: use had + past participle.
Leaving out ‘been’: the form is had been + -ing.
A question about duration before a past point starts with ‘Had’, not ‘Did’: Had + you + been + -ing?
After ‘had been’ use the -ing form.
Looking back from a past point needs had been, not has been.
‘Two years’ is a length of time, so use ‘for’. ‘Since’ needs a starting point, like ‘since 2020’.
The negative goes after ‘had’: hadn’t been working (or had not been working).
In a question, ‘had’ goes before the subject: How long had they been waiting?
Leaving out ‘been’: the form is had been + -ing.
The other past action is in the past simple: ‘when she came home’, not ‘will come’.
‘Belong’ is a state verb: use had + past participle, ‘had belonged’.
‘Own’ is a state verb: use had + past participle, ‘had owned’.
Leaving out ‘been’: the form is had been + -ing.
The past perfect continuous needs ‘had’ before ‘been’: had been waiting.
After ‘had been’ use the -ing form.
Looking back from a past point needs had been, not have been.
‘Lunch’ is a starting point, not a length of time, so use ‘since’.
